stories.title: India October consumer inflation likely near RBI's top target, poll says
stories.summary: A Reuters poll reported by the Economic Times says India's consumer price inflation for October is expected to be close to the upper end of the Reserve Bank of India's inflation target. The poll attributes the upward pressure mainly to higher food prices. No specific inflation rate or poll details were provided.
stories.why: RBI action or currency-market developments can affect rupee volatility, hedging costs and foreign-exchange conditions for businesses and investors.

stories.title: Families of Britons killed in Spanish wildfire demand inquiry after officials block investigation
stories.summary: A wildfire on 9 July swept through the hillside village of Bédar in Almería, Spain, killing 15 people, including nine British nationals. Relatives said they are disgusted that regional politicians blocked an official commission of inquiry and criticised the lack of an emergency mobile‑phone alert that could have warned residents. The governing People’s Party and Vox rejected the opposition Socialist party’s request for an inquiry.
stories.why: The case highlights concerns about emergency warning systems and political accountability in disaster response.

stories.title: Micron Technology shares fall 17% on Nov. 5 amid AI chip selloff
stories.summary: Micron Technology's stock fell 17.46% to close at $656.39 on November 5, its lowest level in nearly six months, after touching an intraday low of $650. Investors dumped semiconductor and AI-related stocks as concerns grew over the outlook for the AI trade. (Sources: TradingKey, Benzinga)
stories.why: The decline reflects growing investor unease about the outlook for AI-related semiconductors.

stories.title: Canada proposes ban on fees for moving investment accounts
stories.summary: The federal government has released draft regulations that would prohibit Canadian banks from charging fees when a client transfers an investment account to another financial institution. The proposal covers registered accounts such as RRSPs, TFSAs and RESPs, as well as non‑registered investment accounts, and the regulatory impact analysis notes that the fees being eliminated are typically about $150 per account.
stories.why: Eliminating the fees lowers costs for consumers, particularly lower‑income Canadians, and may improve competition for smaller financial firms.

stories.title: Major construction ongoing near Iran missile bases, satellite images suggest
stories.summary: At least 12 other military sites, including missile complexes and air bases, appear to show signs of repairs. New roofs have been built on destroyed buildings at the Kermanshah missile base in western Iran, near the border with Iraq, while damaged buildings and debris have been cleared at the Parchin military complex - which has been repeatedly repaired despite a succession of air strikes - east of the capital.

stories.title: American midterm results will not have an impact on India-US interim trade deal: Sources
stories.summary: The Democrats' sweeping victory in the US midterm elections is unlikely to affect the India-US interim trade agreement, as the pact does not require formal Congressional ratification, sources said. The US midterm election results are unlikely to derail the India-US interim trade deal, but ongoing American tariff investigations remain a key hurdle to finalising the agreement.
stories.why: Trade developments can affect currencies, business costs, market access and the external balance of the economies involved.

stories.title: OpenAI’s GPT‑5.6 Sol helps discover Ubuntu server vulnerability
stories.summary: Max Justicz, CTO of Charge Robotics, used OpenAI’s GPT‑5.6 Sol (released in July through the Daybreak Blue program) to locate a severe vulnerability in Ubuntu that could let attackers take control of servers. He reported the flaw to the Debian Project, which issued a patch; there is no known evidence that the bug has been exploited.
stories.why: Demonstrates that advanced AI models can quickly identify critical software bugs, affecting both defensive security practices and potential attack vectors.
stories.previousTitle: OpenAI released a new cybersecurity model. Is that enough?
stories.previousSummary: Max Justicz, the chief technology officer and co-founder of the startup Charge Robotics, used an OpenAI model to find a severe vulnerability that — if exploited — could allow hackers to take control of servers running Ubuntu, a widely used open source Linux-based operating system. Justicz, who has a hobbyist’s interest in cybersecurity and previously found a vulnerability in the same codebase, told TechCrunch that he found this issue using GPT 5.6 Sol, released in July, through the AI maker’s Daybreak Blue, a program that gives cybersecurity defenders access to powerful frontier models.
